title: Hidden in Plain Sight
summary: A secret is hidden in a dotfile. Learn how 'hidden' files really work and find the flag.
story: You just got access to an old practice machine. The last person left a secret here, but you cannot see it with a normal 'ls'. On Unix, any file whose name starts with a dot is 'hidden' from normal listings. That is not security: it is just a quiet convention. Your job is to look where most people never look.
objective: Find the hidden flag file somewhere under your home folder and submit its contents.
hints: A normal 'ls' hides names that start with a dot. Try 'ls -a' to see them.
Hidden folders can hold more hidden folders. 'ls -a' in each one, or let 'find' do the walking: find . -name '.*'.
The fastest way: search every file for the word FLAG. Try: grep -r FLAG . 2>/dev/null
